summary: The last builder lead reproduced, so I dispatched its formal run. Raising the tick period to 1000 ms — large enough that no `drain_notifiers` pass can fall between the origin's batch flush and the truncation that follows it — changed the outcome from the earlier 80 ms attempt: `append_notify` for entry 33 resolved `Ok(4)` while entry 33 sits at index 2 and index 4 holds entry 35, a shift of two that matches two placeholders for the discarded entries being consumed against the fresh batch's index advances. That is a second mechanism inside the same completion bookkeeping — `reconcile_unconfirmed`'s one-placeholder-per-index mapping, distinct from the arm-order defect — and the submitted probe asserts both forms of the obligation (the returned index equals the entry's true position, and the entry at the returned index is the caller's). The harness now emits an admission event so the comparisons can carry a prerequisite alias, and I recorded rather than smoothed over two details of the local run: the new leader's own call did not resolve `Ok(1)` within its timeout and the origin's decided index was still 0 at the re-synchronisation sample, so the internal ordering is inferred from the endpoints. Incomplete: that receipt is pending; two asserted defects with complete comparison chains and two bounded negatives remain the rest of the record.
